findings.problem: Checkout returns 12 against approved 10; service-price reconciliation policy is unstated.
findings.consequence: Customers receive a result that fails the agreed outcome.
findings.fix: Blocked: choose a core-owned rule for differing service prices, then repair production pricing through the public interface. Do not alter expectedTotal or seed HTTP with 10 merely to hide the failure.
findings.verification: Reuse unchanged local HTTP journey asserting 201/10 before and after; minimally protect the chosen policy through the public checkout boundary.

findings.problem: Three web modules bypass the public core interface, including a resolved storage alias.
findings.principle: UI never touches storage and callers use public core (existing).
findings.consequence: Web callers depend on private adapter details; package exports do not stop relative or aliased imports.
findings.fix: Route web dependencies through core/index.ts; expose a bounded checkout/pricing capability once F-001 policy is resolved. Keep storage private. Preserve supported signatures unless separately reviewed.
findings.verification: Compiler-resolved boundaries must pass. Before adoption, prove allowed public/sibling imports and independent private/alias violations in disposable fixtures; retain checkout acceptance.

findings.problem: Maintained check runs only types; passing units do not establish checkout readiness.
findings.principle: Proposed completion rule: affected approved journeys pass on final inputs; units alone are insufficient.
findings.consequence: Normal check can be green while the approved journey and boundaries fail.
findings.fix: Extend existing npm run check with fail-fast type, unit, boundary and journey commands after selected debt is fixed. Add a short evidence section to DESIGN.md pointing to journey.mjs and approved acceptance. No new verification engine or CI requested.
findings.verification: Prove maintained command on clean control and seeded boundary/acceptance violations; keep known failures visible. Verify using local TypeScript 5.9.3, Node 24.17.0 and npm 11.13.0.

findings.problem: Core a and b form mutual recursive cycle; analyzer rejects it.
findings.principle: Proposed acyclic dependency rule, currently encoded in boundary command.
findings.consequence: Any invocation recurses without termination; full boundary check stays red although checkout does not import these files.
findings.fix: Review intended responsibility and remove unused cycle or implement a nonrecursive owner. Do not silently disable the cycle rule; any deferred debt needs scoped reason and removal condition.
findings.verification: Acyclic compiler graph, deliberate cycle fixture rejection, and unchanged public checkout journey.

findings.problem: Order is defined as a purchase and as UI panel sequence.
findings.consequence: Future naming changes could confuse purchase semantics with display ordering.
findings.fix: Draft only: Order = a customer purchase; Panel sequence = the sequence in which UI panels appear. Await owner confirmation and later exact review; no naming migration.
findings.verification: Review against both existing definitions; apply no terminology bytes without selection.

findings.problem: Public quote test expects 12 without a documented quote-price acceptance case.
findings.principle: Tests protect approved public behaviour; distinct quote policy remains unresolved.
findings.consequence: A green test may lock in implementation output that conflicts with a later checkout pricing decision.
findings.fix: Retain checkout total 10. Block changing quote expectation until its relationship to checkout price is resolved; then use the smallest public contract assertion from that approved source.
findings.verification: Review quote acceptance source and run public unit check plus unchanged checkout HTTP journey.
